label: GO-phase a1-vs-a2 lean: last trial outcome plus belief that S1 is good
terms: (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * np.tanh(belief_lo / 2) ;; (phase == GO) * (belief > 0.5)
explanation: Raw candidate n of unit 29 is near-saturated by phase (D1 ~ +0.98, D2 ~ -0.96; timing alone R^2 0.93) and its magnitude beyond timing lives almost entirely at GO, where it goes up when the agent leans toward a1 / S1 and down when it leans toward a2 / S2. At GO the previous trial matters most: a1 S1 r about +0.56 over the timing mean, a2 S1 r +0.17, and the S2 or unrewarded outcomes -0.03 to -0.39 (a2 S2 u lowest). The ideal-observer belief that S1 is good adds a graded effect (belief decile 0 about -0.24, decile 8 about +0.39), and a sign step at belief 0.5 matters on top of a smooth tanh(belief_lo/2). The 7 observed-only GO terms (previous action, state, reward and their interactions, plus belief) score test R^2 beyond timing 0.66, against an all-cue ceiling of 0.80 and an all-observed ceiling of 0.76; the policy decile alone scores 0.44, so going without the model outputs costs little. The trial before last, D2-phase terms and belief_cover interactions each added <0.01. D1 and D2 residuals are under 0.04. The fitted weights are partly collinear, so read individual term signs with care.

issues: Every factual claim checks out against the profile. The GO residuals by previous trial are a1 S1 r +0.56, a2 S1 r +0.17, the rest -0.03 to -0.39 with a2 S2 u lowest (-0.394). By belief decile the GO residual goes from -0.24 to +0.39. D1/D2 cell residuals are all under 0.04, and the reported test R^2 beyond timing of 0.664 reproduces exactly.

The 7 terms barely beat a plain 8-cell previous-trial table (GO x last_is for each pattern). The table alone scores test 0.648 against 0.664 for the claimed terms. The 5 previous-trial terms alone score only 0.453, so the belief terms are mostly making up for previous-trial cells those 5 terms cannot represent. They add only about 0.02 of information beyond the previous trial, not a substantial graded effect.

Systematic error class: misses on the claimed terms show GO over-prediction after a2 S2 u (-0.172), after a1 S2 r (-0.167) and after a2 S1 r (-0.118), and under-prediction after a1 S1 u (+0.086). These are 0.1-0.17 biases in cells whose total residual is only 0.2-0.4. The full last_is table removes them: all |cell error| <= 0.03.

The belief step interacts with the previous reward, which the label does not mention. Adding (GO)*(belief>0.5)*(prev_reward==1) raises test R^2 from about 0.68 to 0.707. With per-cell last_is terms it reaches 0.719, against an all-observed ceiling of 0.76. Without the step at 0.5, the claimed set falls to 0.550, so the step really is needed.
Trial before last (tv('action',-2), same-state reward streak) and ep_dec x prev_action each add <= 0.01. That agrees with the 'adds nothing' claim.

The worst-fit windows show rare large D2 excursions (actual about -0.05 to -0.17 against a predicted -0.93, during an a2 S1R run late in an episode) and GO under-prediction in long a1 S1 rewarded runs late in an episode. These are sparse and do not shift the D2 cell means.
